title: Why your parents’ appliances lasted decades – and yours don’t
titleZh: 为什么以前的东西怎么也用不坏
summary:
尤斯特·费尔德霍伊曾的母亲有两件格外珍视的家当：一台飞利浦料理机和一台美诺吸尘器。它们没有超出基本功能的设计，也没有非常出众的外观。真正让她满意的是，这两件电器在使用了四十年后，至今仍能完全正常运转。在当今追求快速更迭的消费文化中，这样的情况已十分罕见。根据欧洲环境署的数据，目前一台新型无线吸尘器的平均使用寿命不足五年，而像料理机这样的小型家电，通常也难以使用超过九年。

来源：电讯报；作者：Benedict J Smith；原文发布时间：2025-12-31 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Joost Veldhuizen’s mother has two possessions she is especially fond of: her Philips food processor and her Miele vacuum cleaner. Neither does anything beyond their standard functions, nor are they particularly impressive to look at. Their joy stems from the fact that after 40 years of use, both appliances remain in full working order. In today’s fast-paced consumer culture, this is a rarity. The average lifespan of a new cordless vacuum cleaner is less than five years, while small household appliances such as food processors cannot be expected to last more than nine, according to the European Environment Agency.
paragraphs.contentZh: 尤斯特·费尔德霍伊曾的母亲有两件格外珍视的家当：一台飞利浦料理机和一台美诺吸尘器。它们没有超出基本功能的设计，也没有非常出众的外观。真正让她满意的是，这两件电器在使用了四十年后，至今仍能完全正常运转。在当今追求快速更迭的消费文化中，这样的情况已十分罕见。根据欧洲环境署的数据，目前一台新型无线吸尘器的平均使用寿命不足五年，而像料理机这样的小型家电，通常也难以使用超过九年。

paragraphs.contentEn: This has driven the rise of a throwaway culture worldwide. The United Nations estimates that the global volume of discarded electronic goods – known as e-waste – will rise to 82 million tonnes by 2030, up from 62 million in 2022. Veldhuizen – who as a board member of Repair Cafe International, a global network of DIY workshops, has seen his fair share of broken appliances – says we are not just imagining the declining durability of everyday goods. “Quality everywhere appears to be dropping,” he says. “The difficulty these days is when you buy an expensive product, it’s not automatically a guarantee that it will last you a lifetime.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 这在全球范围内助推了用完即弃的消费文化。据联合国估计，全球被丢弃的电子产品（即电子垃圾）总量从2022年的6200万吨，将上升至2030年的8200万吨。作为“国际维修咖啡馆”（该组织是一个由DIY维修工坊组成的全球网络）董事会成员，费尔德霍伊曾长期接触大量故障电器，他认为，人们对于日用品耐用性下降的感受并不是错觉。他说道：“几乎所有品类的产品质量都在下滑。现下的问题在于，即便选购价格不菲的产品，也不一定能够保证它可以用一辈子。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Veldhuizen first points the finger at the growing intensity of rivalries between companies, particularly since the advent of e-commerce. As competition hots up, it can trigger a race to the bottom, with manufacturers engaging in aggressive price-cutting to boost profits and keep shareholders happy. The theory goes that as corners are cut to keep down costs, quality inevitably suffers. British shoemaker Dr Martens, for example, faced a flood of accusations about the falling durability of its famously hardy footwear since it outsourced 98pc of its production to Asia, where labour is much cheaper than in the UK.
paragraphs.contentZh: 费尔德霍伊曾首先将原因归结为企业间日益激烈的竞争，尤其是在电子商务兴起之后。随着竞争不断加剧，制造商之间极易陷入逐底竞争：为了提升利润、安抚股东，制造商往往采取激进的降价策略。按照这一逻辑，为压缩成本而四处削减用料，最终不可避免地会损害产品质量。以英国鞋履品牌马丁大夫为例，自该公司将98%的生产外包至劳动力成本明显低于英国的亚洲地区以来，这款一度以耐用著称的品牌便不断遭到有关耐用性下降的指责。

paragraphs.contentEn: But is the standard of workmanship abroad to blame? Veldhuizen thinks not. “China makes what you ask them to make. If you ask them for a high-quality product, you will get a high-quality product. If you ask them for a cheap, low-quality product, that’s what you will get.” Instead, he believes that competition between companies has pushed them into making straightforward goods overly complex. Manufacturers, he says, have started adding bells and whistles to appeal to gadget-loving consumers. These ultimately make products more susceptible to breakage and difficult to fix.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，问题应该归咎于海外的工艺水准吗？费尔德霍伊曾并不这样认为。他说道：“中国工厂会严格按照你的要求生产。如果你要的是高质量产品，那么得到的就会是高质量产品。如果你只要求廉价、低质，那么结果也只能如此。”在他看来，真正的问题在于企业间的竞争压力，迫使制造商将原本结构简单的商品变得过于复杂。他指出，为了吸引追逐新潮功能的消费者，厂家不断为产品增加各种附加设计。而这些多余的部分最终只会增加产品的故障风险，也让维修变得更为困难。

paragraphs.contentEn: On vacuum cleaners, for instance, it is an electrical add-on, such as suction control, that fails after a couple of years of use in the vast majority of cases. “But you don’t need electronic suction control – it’s a gimmick that companies use to differentiate themselves.” Fixing electronic components demands a level of expertise beyond most ordinary appliance users. But even getting into the device in the first place is harder than it used to be. “Whereas in the good old days parts were readily available and there were a couple of regular screws that you could open up to fix the appliance, clean it and close it up again, it’s becoming a lot more difficult.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 以吸尘器为例，绝大多数情况下，使用几年后最先出现故障的，往往正是吸力控制这类电子附加功能。费尔德霍伊曾指出：“电子吸力控制并非必需——更多只是企业用于区分产品的营销手段。”他表示，维修电子元件所需的专业程度，已经超出了大多数普通家电用户的能力范围。而且，即便只是打开设备本身，现在也比过去困难得多。他说道：“早些年，机器上通常只有几颗普通螺丝，拧开后就能进行维修或清洁，之后再装好就行。但现在，这样的操作正变得越来越难。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Because many goods are produced in countries where labour is relatively cheap, the cost of repairing it domestically is often more expensive than buying new – and therefore the product is thrown out and replaced. Cynics are quick to suggest this is all done on purpose as part of a grand plan by manufacturers to encourage us to replace products more frequently – a theory known as “planned obsolescence”. One of the earliest known examples involved lightbulb makers in the mid-1920s. After technological advancements improved the lifespan of the bulb to 2,500 hours, manufacturers realised they “lasted too long”. In response, the world’s leading makers, including Germany’s Osram, the UK’s Associated Electrical Industries and General Electric in America, colluded to intentionally reduce the lifespan of bulbs by 50pc and thereby stimulate repeat purchases.
paragraphs.contentZh: 由于许多商品产自劳动力成本相对较低的国家，在本国进行维修的费用往往高于直接购买新品——因此这些产品常常被丢弃并由新产品取代。对此，批评者很快指出，这一切很可能是厂商有意为之，是他们敦促消费者更频繁更换产品的整体策略的一部分——即所谓的“计划性报废”。已知最早的案例之一发生在20世纪20年代中期的灯泡行业。当时，随着技术进步，灯泡的使用寿命已能提升至2500小时，但制造商随即发现这样的产品“使用寿命过长”。于是，包括德国欧司朗、英国联合电气工业公司以及美国通用电气在内的多家全球主要厂商达成协议，刻意将灯泡的使用寿命缩短50%，以刺激消费者重复购买。

paragraphs.contentEn: However, Kamila Krych, a researcher at the Institute of Environmental Engineering in Zurich, who studied the lifetime of common household appliances for her PhD, is sceptical of arguments around planned obsolescence. “If it was the case that producers were scheming against us to make things less durable, I would expect all products to go down in lifetime at a more or less similar rate. And this is not what we see,” she says. In her study, Krych investigated how the sales and ownership of large household appliances in Norway had evolved since the 1940s. Although the lifespans of fridges, freezers and dishwashers have remained relatively constant, she found that the longevity of ovens and washing machines plummeted in the 1990s and early 2000s. Washing machines dropped from 19.2 to 10.6 years, while ovens fell from 23.6 to 14.3 years.
paragraphs.contentZh: 然而，曾以常见家电使用寿命为博士研究课题的苏黎世环境工程研究所研究员卡米拉·克里奇，对“计划性报废”的说法持怀疑态度。她表示：“如果制造商真的在暗中合谋，刻意降低产品耐用性，那么不同品类产品的寿命理应以大致相同的速度下降。但现实数据并非如此。”在这项研究中，克里奇考察了自20世纪40年代以来挪威大型家用电器的销售与保有情况。她发现，冰箱、冷柜和洗碗机的使用寿命总体保持相对稳定；但烤箱和洗衣机的耐用性，却在20世纪90年代和21世纪初出现明显下滑。具体来看，洗衣机的平均使用年限从19.2年降至10.6年，烤箱则从23.6年降至14.3年。

paragraphs.contentEn: Krych acknowledges that a flood of cheaper products around the turn of the century undoubtedly had a bearing on the quality of household appliances. But her conclusion also stressed the impact of consumer behaviour. “There is a social component to it, not just technical. For example, with washing machines there is clear evidence pointing towards people doing laundry more often. If you run more cycles per year, your washing machine will last fewer years.” The average Norwegian family, for example, ran two washing cycles per week in 1960 compared with eight in 2000 – a symptom of rising living standards, Krych adds.
paragraphs.contentZh: 克里奇承认，在世纪之交大量涌入市场的廉价产品，确实对家用电器的整体质量产生了影响。但她的研究也着重强调了消费者行为的影响。她表示：“这其中也有社会因素，不纯是技术问题。例如，有明确证据表明，人们使用洗衣机的频率已大幅提高。如果一年中运行的洗涤次数更多，洗衣机能够使用的年限自然就会缩短。”克里奇补充称，以挪威家庭为例，1960年平均每周仅洗衣两次，到2000年已增加至八次——这也反映出生活水平的显著提升。

paragraphs.contentEn: Most consumers are also notoriously lazy when it comes to essential maintenance of products, which only accelerates products’ decline. “For cars, regular maintenance is very common and normal for most people,” Veldhuizen says. “But for household appliances, people expect them to run forever without any maintenance. I have a friend who has a coffee machine with an LED that indicates when it needs descaling that’s been flashing for four months.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 在产品的基本维护方面，许多消费者长期以来并不上心，而这只会加速产品的老化。费尔德霍伊曾指出：“对大多数人来说，定期保养汽车是再正常不过的事。但对于家电，人们却期望它们无需任何维护就能一直运转。我有一位朋友，他咖啡机上提示除垢的指示灯已经闪了四个月，他却始终无动于衷。”

paragraphs.contentEn: How, then, can we pull ourselves out of this rut of throwaway culture? Wayne Hubbard, of ReLondon, a waste reduction initiative, wants to see more consumers taking an interest in not only the quality of the products they are buying but how to repair them. “A little bit of knowledge can go a long way,” he says. “It also makes us savvier shoppers in the long run.” Top-down legislation that gives consumers the ability to make more informed purchasing decisions is also a popular solution. France has led the way with its “Repair Index”, added to electrical products since 2021, which scores them on their “repairability”. The idea is twofold: to encourage consumers to choose goods they can repair and for manufacturers to make them easier to fix.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，我们该如何摆脱用完即弃的消费惯性？减废倡议组织ReLondon的韦恩·哈伯德希望，更多消费者不仅能关注所购产品的质量，也能开始留意如何维修它们。他说道：“掌握一点相关知识，就能带来很大的改变。从长远来看，这也会让我们成为更懂行的消费者。”与此同时，通过自上而下的立法为消费者提供更充分的信息，从而帮助其做出更明智的购买决策，也是一种受到广泛关注的解决方案。法国在这方面走在前列，自2021年起，法国在电器产品上引入“维修指数”，根据产品的“可维修性”为其打分。该制度有双重目的：一是引导消费者选择可维修的商品；二是促使制造商提高产品的可修性。

paragraphs.contentEn: It’s a measure Veldhuizen supports – but he says we cannot ignore the fact that fundamental cultural shifts have changed the dynamic between people and products, possibly for good. “In the 1950s and ’60s, everything was scarce, everything was in short supply and expensive. You had to make do with your things for as long as possible. Now, things have become cheap. We have more money than our parents.” For better or worse, he concedes, the days of sewing up holes in socks are probably over.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这一举措得到了费尔德霍伊曾的支持——但他同时提醒，我们不应忽视一个事实：根本性的文化变迁已经改变了人与物品之间的关系，而且这种变化可能是长期性的。他说道：“在20世纪50至60年代，一切都很稀缺，物资短缺且价格昂贵，人们必须尽可能长时间地使用手头的物品。如今，商品变得便宜，我们的收入也远高于父辈。”他承认，不管怎样，那种袜子破了还要缝补的日子，大概是一去不复返了。
